q.hi: Paytm wallet me money transfer: ek account se debit aur doosre me credit dono ek saath hone chahiye, ya dono fail. Primary DB kaunsa?
q.en: Paytm wallet transfer: debit one account and credit another, both must succeed or both fail. Which primary DB?

hi: PostgreSQL / MySQL (relational, ACID transactions)
Redis (in-memory, fast)
Elasticsearch (fast search)
Cassandra with consistency ONE
en: PostgreSQL / MySQL (relational, ACID transactions)
Redis (in-memory, fast)
Elasticsearch (fast search)
Cassandra with consistency ONE

why.hi: Money movement me multi-row atomic transaction chahiye. Relational DB ka ACID ye seedha deta hai; baaki options me ye guarantee nahi milti.
why.en: Money movement needs an atomic multi-row transaction. Relational ACID gives this directly; the other options do not guarantee it.

q.hi: Swiggy app me "panner tikka" (typo) search karne pe bhi "Paneer Tikka" dishes aani chahiye, relevance ranking ke saath. Kya use karoge?
q.en: In Swiggy, searching "panner tikka" (typo) should still return "Paneer Tikka" dishes with relevance ranking. What do you use?

hi: PostgreSQL me WHERE name = ? exact match
Elasticsearch (fuzzy match + BM25 scoring), source of truth alag DB me
Redis HASH me dish name as key
DynamoDB Scan with contains() filter
en: PostgreSQL WHERE name = ? exact match
Elasticsearch (fuzzy match + BM25 scoring), source of truth in a separate DB
Redis HASH keyed by dish name
DynamoDB Scan with a contains() filter

why.hi: Typo tolerance aur relevance ranking search engine ka kaam hai (inverted index, fuzziness, scoring). ES ko secondary index ki tarah sync karo.
why.en: Typo tolerance and relevance ranking are a search engine job (inverted index, fuzziness, scoring). Keep ES as a synced secondary index.

q.hi: Uber: lakhon drivers har 4 second me location bhejte hain aur rider ke paas "nearby drivers" chahiye. Live location ke liye best fit?
q.en: Uber: lakhs of drivers send location every 4 seconds and riders need "nearby drivers". Best fit for live location?

hi: Neo4j graph me driver nodes
S3 me har update ek naya object
Redis GEO (GEOADD / GEOSEARCH), in-memory, latest location overwrite
Har update ke liye Postgres me naya row INSERT karke full table scan
en: Neo4j graph with driver nodes
A new S3 object per update
Redis GEO (GEOADD / GEOSEARCH), in-memory, latest location overwritten
INSERT a new Postgres row per update and full-scan the table

why.hi: Bahut high write rate, sirf latest value chahiye, aur radius query: in-memory geo index (Redis GEO) ye sab sasta deta hai. History chahiye to alag se stream/TSDB me daalo.
why.en: Very high write rate, only latest value matters, plus radius queries: an in-memory geo index (Redis GEO) does this cheaply. Send history to a stream/TSDB separately.

q.hi: Interview me "naye product ke liye DB choose karo" pe sabse strong approach kaunsi hai?
q.en: In an interview, what is the strongest approach to "choose a DB for a new product"?

hi: MongoDB lo kyunki schema-less hai, future changes easy honge
Cassandra lo kyunki aage chal ke scale chahiye hoga
Ek hi DB sab kaam ke liye, kabhi doosra DB mat jodo
Pehle access patterns, consistency need, read/write ratio aur scale likho; default relational, specific need pe specialised DB add karo
en: Pick MongoDB because schema-less makes future changes easy
Pick Cassandra because you will need scale later
Use one DB for everything and never add another
First list access patterns, consistency needs, read/write ratio and scale; default to relational, add a specialised DB for a specific need

why.hi: DB choice access patterns aur guarantees se nikalti hai, trend se nahi. Postgres sensible default hai; search, cache, analytics jaise needs ke liye purpose-built store jodo.
why.en: DB choice follows access patterns and guarantees, not trends. Postgres is a sensible default; add purpose-built stores for needs like search, cache, analytics.

q.hi: orders table rows (id, amount): (1,100), (2,200), (3,50), (4,NULL). Output of: SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(amount), SUM(amount) FROM orders;
q.en: orders table rows (id, amount): (1,100), (2,200), (3,50), (4,NULL). Output of: SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(amount), SUM(amount) FROM orders;

hi: 4, 3, NULL
en: 4, 3, NULL

why.hi: COUNT(*) saari rows ginta hai (4). COUNT(amount) aur SUM NULL ko ignore karte hain: 3 aur 350.
why.en: COUNT(*) counts all rows (4). COUNT(amount) and SUM ignore NULLs: 3 and 350.

q.hi: users: 1,2,3. orders: user 1 ke 2 orders, user 2 ka 1, user 3 ka koi nahi. SELECT u.id, COUNT(o.id) FROM users u LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = u.id GROUP BY u.id; output?
q.en: users: 1,2,3. orders: user 1 has 2, user 2 has 1, user 3 has none. SELECT u.id, COUNT(o.id) FROM users u LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.user_id = u.id GROUP BY u.id; output?

hi: 3 rows: 1→2, 2→1, 3→NULL
en: 3 rows: 1→2, 2→1, 3→NULL

why.hi: LEFT JOIN user 3 ko rakhta hai with o.id = NULL. COUNT(o.id) NULL nahi ginta, isliye 0. COUNT(*) likhte to 1 aata.
why.en: LEFT JOIN keeps user 3 with o.id = NULL. COUNT(o.id) skips NULL, so 0. COUNT(*) would give 1.

q.hi: PostgreSQL me ek table pe bahut UPDATE hote hain aur table ka size badhta jaata hai jabki row count same hai. Kyu?
q.en: In PostgreSQL a table gets many UPDATEs and keeps growing while the row count stays the same. Why?

hi: WAL file table ke andar merge hoti rehti hai
B-tree index ka rebalancing fail ho jaata hai
Postgres in-place update karta hai jisse fragmentation hota hai
MVCC har UPDATE pe naya row version likhta hai; purane dead tuples VACUUM hone tak jagah lete hain
en: The WAL file keeps getting merged into the table
B-tree index rebalancing fails
Postgres updates in place, which causes fragmentation
MVCC writes a new row version on every UPDATE; old dead tuples take space until VACUUM

why.hi: Postgres MVCC me UPDATE = naya tuple + purana dead. Autovacuum dead tuples reclaim karta hai; agar wo peeche reh jaaye to bloat hota hai.
why.en: In Postgres MVCC, UPDATE = new tuple + old one dead. Autovacuum reclaims dead tuples; if it falls behind, you get bloat.

q.hi: SELECT user_id, SUM(amount) FROM orders WHERE SUM(amount) > 1000 GROUP BY user_id; kya hoga?
q.en: SELECT user_id, SUM(amount) FROM orders WHERE SUM(amount) > 1000 GROUP BY user_id; what happens?

hi: Error: aggregate WHERE me allowed nahi; HAVING SUM(amount) > 1000 use karo
Sahi chalega, 1000 se zyada spend wale users aayenge
Har row ka apna SUM check hoga
Empty result aayega bina error ke
en: Error: aggregates are not allowed in WHERE; use HAVING SUM(amount) > 1000
Works fine and returns users who spent over 1000
Each row is checked against its own SUM
Returns an empty result with no error

why.hi: WHERE grouping se pehle rows filter karta hai, tab tak SUM bana hi nahi. Group ke baad filter HAVING se hota hai.
why.en: WHERE filters rows before grouping, when SUM does not exist yet. Filtering after grouping is done with HAVING.

q.hi: T1 ne balance 500 padha. T2 ne balance 300 kiya aur commit kiya. T1 same transaction me dobara padhta hai to 300 milta hai. Ye anomaly kya hai?
q.en: T1 reads balance 500. T2 sets it to 300 and commits. T1 reads again in the same transaction and gets 300. What anomaly is this?

hi: Dirty read
Phantom read
Non-repeatable read
Lost update
en: Dirty read
Phantom read
Non-repeatable read
Lost update

why.hi: Same row dobara padhne pe committed change dikhna non-repeatable read hai. Dirty read uncommitted data hota; phantom naye rows ka aana hai.
why.en: Seeing a committed change when re-reading the same row is a non-repeatable read. Dirty read is uncommitted data; phantom is new rows appearing.

q.hi: Hospital on-call: rule hai kam se kam 1 doctor on-call. Do doctors ek saath check karte hain (count = 2) aur dono khud ko off kar dete hain, dono commit. Postgres me kaunsa isolation level isse rokega?
q.en: Hospital on-call: at least 1 doctor must stay on call. Two doctors concurrently check (count = 2) and both take themselves off, both commit. Which Postgres isolation level prevents this?

hi: REPEATABLE READ (snapshot isolation)
READ COMMITTED
READ UNCOMMITTED
SERIALIZABLE
en: REPEATABLE READ (snapshot isolation)
READ COMMITTED
READ UNCOMMITTED
SERIALIZABLE

why.hi: Ye write skew hai: dono alag rows likhte hain, isliye snapshot isolation conflict nahi pakadta. Postgres SERIALIZABLE (SSI) ise detect karke ek ko abort karta hai; ya SELECT ... FOR UPDATE se lock lo.
why.en: This is write skew: each writes a different row, so snapshot isolation sees no conflict. Postgres SERIALIZABLE (SSI) detects it and aborts one; or lock with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE.

q.hi: Default isolation levels ke baare me kaunsa sahi hai?
q.en: Which statement about default isolation levels is correct?

hi: PostgreSQL ka default READ COMMITTED, MySQL InnoDB ka REPEATABLE READ
Dono ka default SERIALIZABLE
PostgreSQL ka REPEATABLE READ, MySQL ka READ COMMITTED
Dono ka default READ UNCOMMITTED
en: PostgreSQL defaults to READ COMMITTED, MySQL InnoDB to REPEATABLE READ
Both default to SERIALIZABLE
PostgreSQL defaults to REPEATABLE READ, MySQL to READ COMMITTED
Both default to READ UNCOMMITTED

why.hi: Postgres default READ COMMITTED hai; MySQL InnoDB default REPEATABLE READ (next-key locks ke saath). Interview me ye fark poocha jaata hai.
why.en: Postgres defaults to READ COMMITTED; MySQL InnoDB to REPEATABLE READ (with next-key locks). Interviewers ask about this difference.

q.hi: READ COMMITTED me do requests ek saath balance 500 padhti hain, app 100 ghata ke dono 400 likhti hain. Sahi fix?
q.en: Under READ COMMITTED two requests both read balance 500, the app subtracts 100 and both write 400. Correct fix?

hi: wallet id pe index bana do
Atomic UPDATE wallet SET balance = balance - 100 WHERE id = ? AND balance >= 100 (ya SELECT ... FOR UPDATE)
Connection pool size badha do
READ UNCOMMITTED kar do taaki latest value dikhe
en: Add an index on wallet id
Atomic UPDATE wallet SET balance = balance - 100 WHERE id = ? AND balance >= 100 (or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE)
Increase the connection pool size
Switch to READ UNCOMMITTED to see the latest value

why.hi: Ye lost update hai (read-modify-write race). DB ke andar atomic update ya row lock se dono debit sahi lagte hain; affected rows 0 = insufficient balance.
why.en: This is a lost update (read-modify-write race). An atomic in-DB update or a row lock applies both debits; 0 affected rows = insufficient balance.

q.hi: Index hai (city, cuisine, rating). Kaunsi query ko leftmost-prefix rule ke hisaab se index seek ka fayda NAHI milega?
q.en: Index on (city, cuisine, rating). Which query does NOT get an index seek under the leftmost-prefix rule?

hi: WHERE city = 'Pune'
WHERE city = 'Pune' AND cuisine = 'Chinese'
WHERE city = 'Pune' AND cuisine = 'Chinese' AND rating > 4
WHERE cuisine = 'Chinese' AND rating > 4
en: WHERE city = 'Pune'
WHERE city = 'Pune' AND cuisine = 'Chinese'
WHERE city = 'Pune' AND cuisine = 'Chinese' AND rating > 4
WHERE cuisine = 'Chinese' AND rating > 4

why.hi: Composite B-tree pehle city se sorted hai. city skip karoge to seek ke liye starting point nahi milta (skip-scan jaise special cases chhod ke).
why.en: A composite B-tree is sorted by city first. Skip city and there is no starting point to seek from (special cases like skip scan aside).

q.hi: email pe index hai, phir bhi WHERE LOWER(email) = 'a@b.com' slow hai aur EXPLAIN seq scan dikhata hai. Kyu?
q.en: There is an index on email, but WHERE LOWER(email) = 'a@b.com' is slow and EXPLAIN shows a seq scan. Why?

hi: Column pe function lagaya hai; index raw email ka hai. Expression index LOWER(email) banao
Index corrupt ho gaya hai, REINDEX karo
Email column pe index ban hi nahi sakta
Query me LIMIT nahi hai isliye index skip hua
en: A function wraps the column; the index stores raw email. Create an expression index on LOWER(email)
The index is corrupt, run REINDEX
Indexes cannot be built on an email column
The query has no LIMIT so the index is skipped

why.hi: Index sorted values store karta hai; LOWER(email) alag value hai. Expression/functional index ya data ko lowercase me store karna fix hai.
why.en: The index stores sorted raw values; LOWER(email) is a different value. Fix with an expression index or store emails lowercased.

q.hi: orders.status pe index hai; 90% rows 'DELIVERED' hain. WHERE status = 'DELIVERED' pe planner seq scan choose karta hai. Kyu?
q.en: orders.status is indexed; 90% of rows are 'DELIVERED'. For WHERE status = 'DELIVERED' the planner picks a seq scan. Why?

hi: Planner ka bug hai, hint dena zaroori hai
Low selectivity: itni rows ke liye index + random heap reads, seq scan se mehnga padta hai
Text columns pe index use nahi hota
Index sirf UNIQUE columns pe kaam karta hai
en: It is a planner bug, you must add a hint
Low selectivity: for so many rows, index + random heap reads cost more than a seq scan
Indexes are never used on text columns
Indexes only work on UNIQUE columns

why.hi: Index tab jeetta hai jab kam rows match hon. Rare value (jaise PENDING) ke liye index use hoga; common value ke liye seq scan sasta hai. Partial index bhi option hai.
why.en: An index wins when few rows match. For a rare value (like PENDING) it is used; for a common value a seq scan is cheaper. A partial index is also an option.

q.hi: Query: SELECT amount FROM orders WHERE user_id = ? ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 10. Index (user_id, created_at) INCLUDE (amount) ka extra fayda kya hai?
q.en: Query: SELECT amount FROM orders WHERE user_id = ? ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 10. What extra gain does index (user_id, created_at) INCLUDE (amount) give?

hi: amount pe range filter fast ho jaata hai
Writes fast ho jaate hain kyunki index chhota hai
Covering index: index-only scan, table (heap) tak jaana nahi padta aur sort bhi nahi
user_id unique ban jaata hai
en: Range filters on amount become fast
Writes get faster because the index is smaller
Covering index: index-only scan with no heap lookups and no sort
user_id becomes unique

why.hi: Saare required columns index me hain, to rows table se fetch nahi karni padti; (user_id, created_at) order se sort bhi free. Cost: bada index aur slower writes.
why.en: All needed columns are in the index, so no table fetch; the (user_id, created_at) order makes the sort free. Cost: bigger index and slower writes.

q.hi: Dream11 contest leaderboard: score update hote rehte hain, top 10 chahiye. Redis me kaunsa data structure?
q.en: Dream11 contest leaderboard: scores keep updating, you need the top 10. Which Redis data structure?

hi: Sorted Set: ZADD / ZINCRBY aur ZREVRANGE key 0 9 WITHSCORES
List: LPUSH aur LRANGE 0 9
Hash: HSET aur HGETALL
Set: SADD aur SMEMBERS
en: Sorted Set: ZADD / ZINCRBY and ZREVRANGE key 0 9 WITHSCORES
List: LPUSH and LRANGE 0 9
Hash: HSET and HGETALL
Set: SADD and SMEMBERS

why.hi: Sorted Set score ke hisaab se sorted rehta hai; update O(log N) aur top-K range read sasta. List/Hash/Set khud sort nahi karte.
why.en: A Sorted Set stays ordered by score; updates are O(log N) and top-K range reads are cheap. List/Hash/Set do not sort by score.

q.hi: Redis se order 123 pe 30 second ka distributed lock lena hai. Sahi command?
q.en: You need a 30-second distributed lock on order 123 in Redis. Correct command?

hi: SETNX lock:order:123 1 phir alag se EXPIRE lock:order:123 30
SET lock:order:123 <unique-token> NX PX 30000
GET lock:order:123, khaali ho to SET lock:order:123 1
INCR lock:order:123 bina expiry ke
en: SETNX lock:order:123 1 then a separate EXPIRE lock:order:123 30
SET lock:order:123 <unique-token> NX PX 30000
GET lock:order:123 and SET it to 1 if empty
INCR lock:order:123 with no expiry

why.hi: SET NX PX ek atomic step me "nahi hai to set karo + TTL" karta hai. SETNX+EXPIRE ke beech crash = lock kabhi expire nahi; GET-then-SET me race hai. Release pe token match karke delete karo.
why.en: SET NX PX does "set if absent + TTL" atomically. A crash between SETNX and EXPIRE leaves a lock that never expires; GET-then-SET races. On release, delete only if the token matches.

q.hi: DynamoDB orders table: partition key user_id, sort key order_ts. User ke latest 10 orders kaise laaoge?
q.en: DynamoDB orders table: partition key user_id, sort key order_ts. How do you fetch a user's latest 10 orders?

hi: Scan with FilterExpression user_id = :u, Limit = 10
GetItem with user_id only
Query with KeyConditionExpression user_id = :u, ScanIndexForward = false, Limit = 10
Scan the full table and sort in the app
en: Scan with FilterExpression user_id = :u, Limit = 10
GetItem with user_id only
Query with KeyConditionExpression user_id = :u, ScanIndexForward = false, Limit = 10
Scan the full table and sort in the app

why.hi: Query ek partition padhta hai, sort key order me; ScanIndexForward=false = descending. Scan poori table padhta hai aur filter baad me lagta hai (Limit filter se pehle lagta hai). GetItem ko poori primary key chahiye.
why.en: Query reads one partition in sort key order; ScanIndexForward=false = descending. Scan reads the whole table and filters afterwards (Limit applies before the filter). GetItem needs the full primary key.

q.hi: DynamoDB me partition key = order_date rakha. Sale day pe saare writes throttle ho rahe hain jabki table ki total capacity bahut hai. Fix?
q.en: DynamoDB partition key = order_date. On sale day all writes throttle even though total table capacity is high. Fix?

hi: Table ka provisioned capacity aur badha do, bas
order_date ko sort key bana do aur partition key hata do
Global Secondary Index on order_date bana do
High-cardinality key lo ya write sharding karo (order_date#0..N suffix) taaki writes partitions me spread hon
en: Just raise the table provisioned capacity further
Make order_date the sort key and drop the partition key
Create a Global Secondary Index on order_date
Use a high-cardinality key or write sharding (order_date#0..N suffix) so writes spread across partitions

why.hi: Ek din ke saare writes ek partition key pe = hot partition; har partition ki apni throughput limit hai. Suffix se spread karo, read pe saare suffixes query karke merge karo. Partition key compulsory hai.
why.en: All writes for one day hit one partition key = hot partition; each partition has its own throughput limit. Spread with a suffix and query all suffixes on read. A partition key is mandatory.

q.hi: MongoDB me kis data ko parent document me embed NAHI karna chahiye?
q.en: In MongoDB, which data should NOT be embedded in the parent document?

hi: Order ke line items (bounded, saath me padhe jaate hain)
Viral post ke comments (unbounded, lakhon tak badh sakte hain)
User ka shipping address (chhota, saath me padha jaata hai)
Product ke 5 size variants
en: Order line items (bounded, read together)
Comments on a viral post (unbounded, can grow to lakhs)
A user's shipping address (small, read together)
A product's 5 size variants

why.hi: Unbounded arrays document ko 16 MB limit tak le jaate hain aur har update bhaari karte hain. Comments alag collection me postId reference ke saath rakho.
why.en: Unbounded arrays push the document towards the 16 MB limit and make every update heavy. Keep comments in a separate collection referencing postId.

q.hi: MongoDB me ek single document ka maximum size kitna hai?
q.en: What is the maximum size of a single MongoDB document?

hi: 1 MB
64 MB
16 MB
Koi limit nahi
en: 1 MB
64 MB
16 MB
No limit

why.hi: BSON document limit 16 MB hai; isse bade files ke liye GridFS ya S3 use karo. (1 MB Firestore aur 400 KB DynamoDB item limit hai.)
why.en: The BSON document limit is 16 MB; for bigger files use GridFS or S3. (Firestore's limit is 1 MB; DynamoDB items are 400 KB.)

q.hi: Firestore: where('city', '==', 'Pune').orderBy('rating', 'desc') chalane pe error aata hai jisme index banane ka link hai. Kyu?
q.en: Firestore: where('city', '==', 'Pune').orderBy('rating', 'desc') fails with an error containing a link to create an index. Why?

hi: Firestore orderBy support hi nahi karta
city field string hai isliye filter nahi hota
Ek query me sirf ek document return hota hai
Equality filter + alag field pe orderBy ke liye composite index chahiye
en: Firestore does not support orderBy at all
city is a string so it cannot be filtered
A query can return only one document
An equality filter plus orderBy on another field needs a composite index

why.hi: Firestore har query index se serve karta hai; single-field index auto bante hain, multi-field combos ke liye composite index declare karna padta hai.
why.en: Firestore serves every query from an index; single-field indexes are automatic, multi-field combinations need a declared composite index.

q.hi: Query: db.orders.find({ userId: 42 }).sort({ createdAt: -1 }).limit(10). Best index?
q.en: Query: db.orders.find({ userId: 42 }).sort({ createdAt: -1 }).limit(10). Best index?

hi: { userId: 1, createdAt: -1 }
{ createdAt: -1, userId: 1 }
Sirf { userId: 1 }
Do alag indexes: { userId: 1 } aur { createdAt: -1 }
en: { userId: 1, createdAt: -1 }
{ createdAt: -1, userId: 1 }
Only { userId: 1 }
Two separate indexes: { userId: 1 } and { createdAt: -1 }

why.hi: ESR rule: Equality field pehle, phir Sort field. Is index se user ke docs pehle se createdAt order me milte hain, in-memory sort nahi. Sirf userId wale index me sort memory me hoga.
why.en: ESR rule: Equality field first, then the Sort field. This index returns the user's docs already in createdAt order, no in-memory sort. With only userId the sort runs in memory.

q.hi: Cassandra, replication factor N = 3. Kaunsa combination guarantee karta hai ki read latest successful write dekhe?
q.en: Cassandra, replication factor N = 3. Which combination guarantees a read sees the latest successful write?

hi: W = ONE, R = ONE
W = ONE, R = QUORUM (2)
W = QUORUM (2), R = QUORUM (2)
W = TWO, R = ONE
en: W = ONE, R = ONE
W = ONE, R = QUORUM (2)
W = QUORUM (2), R = QUORUM (2)
W = TWO, R = ONE

why.hi: Strong read ke liye R + W > N. 2 + 2 = 4 > 3, to read aur write replicas overlap karte hain. Baaki sab ka sum 2 ya 3 hai, jo > 3 nahi.
why.en: A strong read needs R + W > N. 2 + 2 = 4 > 3, so read and write replicas overlap. The others sum to 2 or 3, not > 3.

q.hi: WhatsApp-type app: "ek chat ke messages, latest pehle" query ke liye Cassandra table ka primary key?
q.en: WhatsApp-like app: for the query "messages of one chat, latest first", what Cassandra primary key?

hi: PRIMARY KEY ((sent_at), chat_id)
PRIMARY KEY ((chat_id, sent_at))
PRIMARY KEY (message_id) aur chat_id pe secondary index
PRIMARY KEY ((chat_id), sent_at) WITH CLUSTERING ORDER BY (sent_at DESC)
en: PRIMARY KEY ((sent_at), chat_id)
PRIMARY KEY ((chat_id, sent_at))
PRIMARY KEY (message_id) with a secondary index on chat_id
PRIMARY KEY ((chat_id), sent_at) WITH CLUSTERING ORDER BY (sent_at DESC)

why.hi: Partition key = chat_id taaki ek chat ek partition me ho; clustering key sent_at DESC se rows already sorted. Bahut busy chats ke liye (chat_id, day) bucket karo.
why.en: Partition key = chat_id keeps a chat in one partition; clustering key sent_at DESC keeps rows sorted. For very busy chats bucket by (chat_id, day).

q.hi: Cassandra writes itne fast kyu hote hain?
q.en: Why are Cassandra writes so fast?

hi: Write sirf commit log me append + memtable me jaata hai; SSTables baad me flush hote hain, read-before-write nahi
Har write se pehle B-tree page in-place update hota hai
Writes sirf ek master node pe jaate hain
Writes disk pe jaate hi nahi, sirf RAM me rehte hain
en: A write is just a commit log append + memtable insert; SSTables are flushed later, no read-before-write
Each write updates a B-tree page in place first
Writes go to a single master node only
Writes never reach disk, they stay in RAM only

why.hi: LSM-style write path: sequential commit log (durability) + memtable; full hone pe immutable SSTable flush, compaction baad me merge karta hai.
why.en: LSM-style write path: sequential commit log (durability) + memtable; when full it flushes to an immutable SSTable, and compaction merges later.

q.hi: Cassandra table ko queue ki tarah use kiya: rows insert karke process hone pe DELETE. Kuch time baad reads bahut slow aur timeouts. Root cause?
q.en: A Cassandra table is used as a queue: insert rows, DELETE after processing. Later reads become very slow with timeouts. Root cause?

hi: Commit log full ho gaya
Deletes tombstones banate hain jo gc_grace_seconds tak rehte hain; reads ko hazaron tombstones scan karne padte hain
Replication factor bahut kam hai
Partition key me hashing band ho gayi
en: The commit log is full
Deletes create tombstones that live until gc_grace_seconds; reads must scan thousands of tombstones
The replication factor is too low
Hashing of the partition key got disabled

why.hi: Cassandra me delete bhi ek write (tombstone) hai. Queue pattern me partition tombstones se bhar jaata hai. Queue ke liye Kafka/SQS lo, ya time-bucketed partitions + TTL.
why.en: In Cassandra a delete is also a write (tombstone). A queue pattern fills partitions with tombstones. Use Kafka/SQS for queues, or time-bucketed partitions + TTL.

q.hi: Flipkart: brand field pe exact filter aur terms aggregation (brand-wise count) chahiye. Elasticsearch mapping?
q.en: Flipkart: you need exact filters and a terms aggregation (count per brand) on the brand field. Elasticsearch mapping?

hi: text
text with standard analyzer only
nested
keyword
en: text
text with standard analyzer only
nested
keyword

why.hi: keyword value ko as-is ek token rakhta hai: exact match, sorting, aggregations. text analyze hota hai (tokens) aur full-text search ke liye hai. Dono chahiye to multi-field (text + .keyword).
why.en: keyword stores the value as one exact token: exact match, sorting, aggregations. text is analyzed into tokens for full-text search. Need both? Use a multi-field (text + .keyword).

q.hi: title field "text" type hai. term query { "term": { "title": "Samsung Galaxy" } } koi result nahi deti, jabki doc me title "Samsung Galaxy S24" hai. Kyu?
q.en: title is a "text" field. The term query { "term": { "title": "Samsung Galaxy" } } returns nothing, though a doc has title "Samsung Galaxy S24". Why?

hi: Index me title lowercase tokens (samsung, galaxy, s24) me store hai; term query input ko analyze nahi karti
term query sirf numbers pe kaam karti hai
Document abhi tak replicate nahi hua
ES case-sensitive nahi hai isliye match fail hua
en: The index stores title as lowercase tokens (samsung, galaxy, s24); a term query does not analyze its input
term queries only work on numbers
The document has not replicated yet
ES is not case-sensitive so the match failed

why.hi: Text field pe match query use karo (wo input ko bhi analyze karti hai). term exact keyword fields ke liye hai.
why.en: Use a match query on text fields (it analyzes the input too). term is for exact keyword fields.

q.hi: Elasticsearch ka inverted index kya map karta hai?
q.en: What does an Elasticsearch inverted index map?

hi: Har document → uske saare fields
Har term → us term wale documents ki list (postings)
Har shard → uske replicas
Har query → uska cached result
en: Each document → all of its fields
Each term → the list of documents containing it (postings)
Each shard → its replicas
Each query → its cached result

why.hi: Book ke index jaisa: word se seedha matching doc IDs. Isliye full-text search poori docs scan kiye bina fast hota hai.
why.en: Like a book index: from a word straight to matching doc IDs. That is why full-text search is fast without scanning all docs.

q.hi: Product ko ES me index karte hi turant search kiya, result nahi aaya; 1 second baad aa gaya. Kyu?
q.en: A product is indexed in ES and searched immediately; it is missing, but appears 1 second later. Why?

hi: Index request fail hui aur retry hui
Primary shard aur replica ka data alag hai permanently
ES near-real-time hai: naya data refresh (default ~1s) ke baad hi searchable segment me aata hai
Inverted index sirf raat ko rebuild hota hai
en: The index request failed and was retried
Primary and replica data differ permanently
ES is near-real-time: new data becomes searchable only after a refresh (default ~1s) opens a new segment
The inverted index is rebuilt only at night

why.hi: Refresh interval ke baad naya segment search ke liye open hota hai. Isliye ES ko source of truth nahi, secondary search index rakho; tests me ?refresh=wait_for use kar sakte ho.
why.en: A new segment opens for search after the refresh interval. So keep ES as a secondary search index, not the source of truth; tests can use ?refresh=wait_for.

q.hi: http_requests_total ek counter hai. Pichhle 5 minute ka per-second request rate kaunsi PromQL dega?
q.en: http_requests_total is a counter. Which PromQL gives the per-second request rate over the last 5 minutes?

hi: rate(http_requests_total[5m])
http_requests_total[5m]
sum(http_requests_total)
delta(http_requests_total[5m])
en: rate(http_requests_total[5m])
http_requests_total[5m]
sum(http_requests_total)
delta(http_requests_total[5m])

why.hi: rate() range vector pe per-second average increase deta hai aur counter resets handle karta hai. [5m] akela sirf raw samples (range vector) hai; delta() gauges ke liye hai.
why.en: rate() gives the per-second average increase over a range vector and handles counter resets. [5m] alone is just raw samples (a range vector); delta() is for gauges.

q.hi: Pod restart hua aur counter 12000 se 0 pe aa gaya. rate(http_requests_total[5m]) kya karega?
q.en: A pod restarted and its counter dropped from 12000 to 0. What does rate(http_requests_total[5m]) do?

hi: Negative rate dikhata hai
Drop ko counter reset maan ke adjust karta hai, isliye negative rate nahi aata
Poori series ko NaN kar deta hai
Restart ke baad ka data ignore karta hai
en: Shows a negative rate
Treats the drop as a counter reset and adjusts, so no negative rate
Turns the whole series into NaN
Ignores data after the restart

why.hi: Counter sirf badhta hai; value girna = reset. rate/increase reset ko detect karke naya value pichhle total pe jod ke calculate karte hain.
why.en: A counter only goes up; a drop means reset. rate/increase detect the reset and treat the new value as added on top of the previous total.

q.hi: Kisi ne Prometheus metric me label user_id add kar diya (crores users). Kya problem hogi?
q.en: Someone added a user_id label to a Prometheus metric (crores of users). What goes wrong?

hi: Kuch nahi, labels free hain
Sirf disk thoda zyada lagega, RAM same
Cardinality explosion: har label combination ek alag series; memory aur query cost bahut badh jaata hai
Prometheus label ko automatically drop kar deta hai
en: Nothing, labels are free
Only slightly more disk, same RAM
Cardinality explosion: each label combination is a separate series; memory and query cost blow up
Prometheus drops the label automatically

why.hi: Har unique label set = nayi time series, jiska index RAM me rehta hai. Labels low-cardinality rakho (service, status, region); per-user data logs/OLAP me.
why.en: Every unique label set = a new time series whose index lives in RAM. Keep labels low-cardinality (service, status, region); per-user data goes to logs/OLAP.

q.hi: Har service ka total request rate chahiye (multiple pods). Sahi PromQL?
q.en: You need total request rate per service (many pods). Correct PromQL?

hi: rate(sum by (service) (http_requests_total)[5m:])
sum by (service) (http_requests_total) / 300
rate(http_requests_total[5m]) without any aggregation
sum by (service) (rate(http_requests_total[5m]))
en: rate(sum by (service) (http_requests_total)[5m:])
sum by (service) (http_requests_total) / 300
rate(http_requests_total[5m]) without any aggregation
sum by (service) (rate(http_requests_total[5m]))

why.hi: Pehle rate (per series), phir sum. Pehle sum karoge to ek pod ka reset sum me drop banta hai jo reset jaisa nahi pakda jaata, aur result galat aata hai.
why.en: Rate first (per series), then sum. Summing first turns one pod's reset into a dip in the sum that rate cannot treat correctly, giving wrong results.

q.hi: Cypher: MATCH (u:User {id: 1})-[:FOLLOWS]->(f)-[:FOLLOWS]->(fof) WHERE NOT (u)-[:FOLLOWS]->(fof) AND fof <> u RETURN DISTINCT fof. Ye kya return karta hai?
q.en: Cypher: MATCH (u:User {id: 1})-[:FOLLOWS]->(f)-[:FOLLOWS]->(fof) WHERE NOT (u)-[:FOLLOWS]->(fof) AND fof <> u RETURN DISTINCT fof. What does it return?

hi: User 1 ke saare followers
User 1 jinko follow karta hai, unke follows jinhe user 1 abhi follow nahi karta (people you may know)
User 1 jinko directly follow karta hai
Jo log user 1 ko follow karte hain par user 1 unhe nahi
en: All followers of user 1
People followed by those user 1 follows, whom user 1 does not follow yet (people you may know)
People user 1 directly follows
People who follow user 1 but user 1 does not follow back

why.hi: Arrow direction u → f → fof hai: 2-hop. WHERE NOT existing follows aur khud ko hata deta hai. Classic recommendation pattern.
why.en: The arrow direction is u → f → fof: 2 hops. WHERE removes existing follows and the user themself. A classic recommendation pattern.

q.hi: Cypher me (a)-[:FRIEND*1..3]->(b) ka matlab?
q.en: In Cypher, what does (a)-[:FRIEND*1..3]->(b) mean?

hi: Exactly 3 FRIEND relationships wale nodes
a ke pehle 3 friends
a se b tak 1 se 3 FRIEND hops ka variable-length path
FRIEND relationship ka weight 1 se 3 ke beech
en: Nodes with exactly 3 FRIEND relationships
The first 3 friends of a
A variable-length path of 1 to 3 FRIEND hops from a to b
A FRIEND relationship with weight between 1 and 3

why.hi: *min..max variable-length traversal hai. Upper bound zaroor do, warna bade graph me query explode ho sakti hai.
why.en: *min..max is variable-length traversal. Always set an upper bound, or the query can explode on a large graph.

q.hi: Deep traversal (4-5 hops) me graph DB relational joins se fast kyu hota hai?
q.en: Why is a graph DB faster than relational joins for deep (4-5 hop) traversals?

hi: Graph DB saara data hamesha GPU pe rakhta hai
Graph DB me SQL se zyada indexes bante hain
Graph DB transactions support nahi karta isliye fast hai
Index-free adjacency: har node apne neighbours ko directly point karta hai, cost visited nodes pe depend karti hai, table size pe nahi
en: Graph DBs always keep all data on a GPU
Graph DBs build more indexes than SQL
Graph DBs skip transactions, which makes them fast
Index-free adjacency: each node points directly to its neighbours, so cost depends on nodes visited, not table size

why.hi: SQL me har hop ek join/index lookup hai jo table size ke saath badhta hai. Graph me relationship pointer follow karna constant-ish cost hai. (Neo4j ACID transactions support karta hai.)
why.en: In SQL each hop is a join/index lookup that grows with table size. In a graph, following a relationship pointer is roughly constant cost. (Neo4j does support ACID transactions.)

q.hi: Kaunsa use case graph DB ke liye sabse kam fit hai?
q.en: Which use case is the poorest fit for a graph DB?

hi: Saare orders ka monthly revenue SUM by city (full-table aggregation)
Paytm me shared devices/accounts se fraud ring dhoondhna
LinkedIn "2nd degree connections"
Swiggy me "users who ordered X also ordered Y" style recommendations
en: Monthly revenue SUM by city across all orders (full-table aggregation)
Finding fraud rings via shared devices/accounts at Paytm
LinkedIn "2nd degree connections"
Swiggy "users who ordered X also ordered Y" style recommendations

why.hi: Graph DB relationships ke traversal me chamakta hai. Poore data pe aggregation OLAP/columnar ka kaam hai.
why.en: Graph DBs shine at traversing relationships. Aggregating over all data is a job for OLAP/columnar stores.

q.hi: HNSW index me efSearch badhane se kya hota hai?
q.en: What happens when you increase efSearch in an HNSW index?

hi: Recall aur latency dono kam hote hain
Index build time kam hota hai, query pe asar nahi
Recall badhta hai, query latency bhi badhti hai
Memory usage aadha ho jaata hai
en: Both recall and latency go down
Index build time drops, queries unaffected
Recall goes up, and query latency goes up too
Memory usage halves

why.hi: efSearch = search ke time candidate list ka size. Bada list = zyada nodes explore = better recall par slow. (M aur efConstruction build-time/memory knobs hain.)
why.en: efSearch = size of the candidate list at query time. Bigger list = more nodes explored = better recall but slower. (M and efConstruction are build-time/memory knobs.)

q.hi: 10 crore embeddings pe exact kNN ki jagah ANN (HNSW/IVF) kyu use karte hain?
q.en: Why use ANN (HNSW/IVF) instead of exact kNN over 10 crore embeddings?

hi: ANN hamesha exact se zyada accurate hai
Exact kNN cosine similarity support nahi karta
ANN ko embeddings store hi nahi karne padte
Exact kNN har query pe saare vectors se distance nikalta hai (O(N·d)); ANN thoda recall chhod ke bahut fast hai
en: ANN is always more accurate than exact
Exact kNN does not support cosine similarity
ANN does not need to store embeddings at all
Exact kNN computes distance to every vector per query (O(N·d)); ANN trades a little recall for big speed

why.hi: Approximate = top-k me kabhi kabhi ek-do sahi neighbours miss ho sakte hain, par latency ms me. Ye recall vs speed trade-off hai.
why.en: Approximate = top-k may occasionally miss a true neighbour or two, but latency is in ms. It is a recall vs speed trade-off.

q.hi: Embeddings L2-normalized (length 1) hain. Kaunsa metric cosine similarity jaisa hi ranking dega?
q.en: Embeddings are L2-normalized (length 1). Which metric gives the same ranking as cosine similarity?

hi: Dot product (inner product)
Manhattan (L1) distance
Hamming distance
Jaccard similarity
en: Dot product (inner product)
Manhattan (L1) distance
Hamming distance
Jaccard similarity

why.hi: cos(a,b) = a·b / (|a||b|); length 1 ho to cos = a·b. Isliye normalized vectors pe inner product sasta aur same ranking deta hai.
why.en: cos(a,b) = a·b / (|a||b|); with length 1, cos = a·b. So on normalized vectors inner product is cheaper and ranks the same.

q.hi: Swiggy semantic dish search: ANN se top 10 nikale, phir city = Pune filter lagaya; sirf 2 results bache. Kyu aur fix?
q.en: Swiggy semantic dish search: take ANN top 10, then filter city = Pune; only 2 results remain. Why, and the fix?

hi: HNSW city field ko index nahi karta isliye bug hai
Post-filtering: top-k pehle bana, filter ne zyada tar hata diye. Pre-filter / filtered ANN use karo ya k bada lo
Embeddings galat dimension ke hain
Cosine ki jagah Euclidean lagao to 10 aa jaayenge
en: HNSW does not index the city field, so it is a bug
Post-filtering: top-k was chosen first and the filter removed most. Use pre-filtering / filtered ANN or fetch a larger k
The embeddings have the wrong dimension
Switch from cosine to Euclidean to get 10

why.hi: Filter ANN ke baad lagaoge to k se kam results aa sakte hain. Vector DBs metadata filter search ke andar (pre/in-filter) support karte hain.
why.en: Filtering after ANN can return fewer than k results. Vector DBs support metadata filtering inside the search (pre/in-filter).

q.hi: Zerodha: arabon trades pe daily P&L aur segment-wise aggregates ki reports. Best store?
q.en: Zerodha: daily P&L and segment-wise aggregate reports over billions of trades. Best store?

hi: Primary OLTP Postgres pe hi heavy GROUP BY
Redis Sorted Sets
MongoDB with embedded trades
Columnar OLAP (ClickHouse / BigQuery / Redshift)
en: Heavy GROUP BY directly on the primary OLTP Postgres
Redis Sorted Sets
MongoDB with embedded trades
Columnar OLAP (ClickHouse / BigQuery / Redshift)

why.hi: Bade scans + aggregations few columns pe = OLAP. Primary OLTP DB pe chalane se live traffic slow hota hai; data CDC/ETL se warehouse me bhejo.
why.en: Large scans + aggregations over a few columns = OLAP. Running them on the primary OLTP DB slows live traffic; ship data via CDC/ETL to a warehouse.

q.hi: SELECT SUM(amount) FROM orders WHERE order_date >= ... (table me 60 columns). Columnar store isme fast kyu hai?
q.en: SELECT SUM(amount) FROM orders WHERE order_date >= ... (table has 60 columns). Why is a columnar store fast here?

hi: Sirf amount aur order_date columns disk se padhe jaate hain, aur same-type column data achha compress hota hai
Har row ek saath padhi jaati hai isliye cache friendly
Columnar DB har query ka result pehle se store rakhta hai
Columnar DB me indexes ki zarurat nahi kyunki data RAM me hai
en: Only the amount and order_date columns are read from disk, and same-type column data compresses well
Each whole row is read at once, which is cache friendly
Columnar DBs pre-store every query result
Columnar DBs need no indexes because data is in RAM

why.hi: Row store ko 60 columns wali poori rows padhni padti. Columnar 2 columns padhta hai, compressed, vectorized execution ke saath.
why.en: A row store would read whole 60-column rows. Columnar reads 2 columns, compressed, with vectorized execution.

q.hi: Columnar DB ko Swiggy ke live order status updates (single row UPDATE, point lookups) ke liye primary kyu nahi banate?
q.en: Why not use a columnar DB as primary for Swiggy live order status updates (single-row UPDATEs, point lookups)?

hi: Columnar DB SQL support nahi karta
Ek row ka data alag-alag column files me hai; single-row update/lookup mehnga hai aur immutable parts rewrite karne padte hain
Columnar DB me data compress nahi hota
Columnar DB sirf ek user ko access deta hai
en: Columnar DBs do not support SQL
One row is spread across separate column files; single-row updates/lookups are costly and immutable parts get rewritten
Columnar DBs do not compress data
Columnar DBs allow only one user

why.hi: Columnar bulk append + scan ke liye optimised hai. Frequent small updates aur point reads OLTP (row store) ka kaam hai.
why.en: Columnar is optimised for bulk appends + scans. Frequent small updates and point reads are OLTP (row store) work.

q.hi: ClickHouse MergeTree me PRIMARY KEY / ORDER BY (restaurant_id, order_date) diya. Kaunsa sahi hai?
q.en: In ClickHouse MergeTree you set PRIMARY KEY / ORDER BY (restaurant_id, order_date). Which is correct?

hi: Ye har row ke liye unique constraint enforce karta hai
Ye B-tree hai jo har row ko point karta hai
Ye sparse index hai (har granule, default 8192 rows, ka ek mark); uniqueness enforce nahi hoti, duplicates allowed
Iska query filtering pe koi asar nahi, sirf storage order
en: It enforces a unique constraint on every row
It is a B-tree pointing to every row
It is a sparse index (one mark per granule, default 8192 rows); uniqueness is not enforced, duplicates are allowed
It does not affect query filtering, only storage order

why.hi: Data ORDER BY ke hisaab se sorted store hota hai aur sparse marks se granules skip hote hain. Dedup ke liye ReplacingMergeTree jaise engines hain (eventual).
why.en: Data is stored sorted by ORDER BY and sparse marks let it skip granules. For dedup there are engines like ReplacingMergeTree (eventual).

q.hi: CockroachDB / Spanner me single-row write, ek single-node Postgres se slow kyu hota hai?
q.en: Why is a single-row write in CockroachDB / Spanner slower than on a single-node Postgres?

hi: Har write ko Raft/Paxos consensus se majority replicas pe commit hona padta hai (multi-region me network RTT)
Ye DBs har write ke baad poora index rebuild karte hain
Inme WAL nahi hota isliye har write fsync bina retry hota hai
Ye DBs har write ko S3 pe upload karte hain
en: Every write must be committed to a majority of replicas via Raft/Paxos consensus (network RTT across regions)
They rebuild the whole index after each write
They have no WAL, so every write retries without fsync
They upload every write to S3

why.hi: Strong consistency + fault tolerance ki keemat: commit ke liye quorum ack chahiye. Replicas door hain to latency zyada; leaseholder/leader ko users ke paas rakho.
why.en: The price of strong consistency + fault tolerance: commit needs a quorum ack. Far replicas mean more latency; place the leaseholder/leader near users.

q.hi: Spanner TrueTime ka "commit wait" kya karta hai?
q.en: What does Spanner TrueTime "commit wait" do?

hi: Sabhi replicas ke clocks ko NTP se sync karta hai
Commit timestamp ke baad clock uncertainty (ε) ke barabar wait karta hai taaki commit order real-time order se match kare (external consistency)
Lock milne tak transaction ko sleep karata hai
Read replicas ko commit hone tak block karta hai
en: It syncs all replica clocks via NTP
After choosing the commit timestamp it waits out the clock uncertainty (ε) so commit order matches real-time order (external consistency)
It sleeps the transaction until a lock is free
It blocks read replicas until commit

why.hi: TrueTime time ko interval [earliest, latest] deta hai. Wait karne se koi bhi baad wali transaction ka timestamp guaranteed bada hota hai. GPS + atomic clocks se ε chhota (few ms).
why.en: TrueTime returns time as an interval [earliest, latest]. Waiting guarantees any later transaction gets a larger timestamp. GPS + atomic clocks keep ε small (a few ms).

q.hi: Kis scenario me NewSQL (Spanner / CockroachDB / YugabyteDB) sabse justified hai?
q.en: In which scenario is NewSQL (Spanner / CockroachDB / YugabyteDB) most justified?

hi: Chhota startup app, ek region, 10 GB data
Logs ka full-text search
Multi-region payments ledger: SQL + strong consistency + horizontal scale + region failure survive karna
Ek session cache with TTL
en: A small startup app, one region, 10 GB of data
Full-text search over logs
A multi-region payments ledger: SQL + strong consistency + horizontal scale + surviving a region failure
A session cache with TTL

why.hi: NewSQL distributed SQL with ACID deta hai par latency aur cost zyada. Chhote single-region workload pe Postgres simple aur fast hai.
why.en: NewSQL gives distributed SQL with ACID but costs latency and money. For a small single-region workload, Postgres is simpler and faster.

q.hi: CockroachDB range ke 5 replicas hain (Raft). Kitne replicas fail hone pe bhi range writes accept karegi?
q.en: A CockroachDB range has 5 replicas (Raft). How many replicas can fail while the range still accepts writes?

why.hi: Raft ko majority chahiye: 5 me se 3. To 2 fail tolerate hote hain. (3 replicas = 1 failure.) Rule: 2f + 1 replicas = f failures.
why.en: Raft needs a majority: 3 of 5. So 2 failures are tolerated. (3 replicas = 1 failure.) Rule: 2f + 1 replicas tolerate f failures.

q.hi: User ne profile name update kiya, refresh pe purana name dikha. Reads replicas se aate hain (async replication). Sahi fix?
q.en: A user updates their profile name and sees the old name on refresh. Reads go to async replicas. Correct fix?

hi: Replicas hata do, sab primary se padho hamesha
Read-your-writes: write ke baad kuch der us user ke reads primary se (ya replica jo us LSN tak pahunch gaya ho)
Cache TTL badha do
Sharding kar do
en: Remove replicas and always read from the primary
Read-your-writes: after a write, serve that user's reads from the primary for a while (or from a replica caught up to that LSN)
Increase the cache TTL
Add sharding

why.hi: Ye replication lag hai. Sirf affected user/time window ko primary pe route karo; baaki reads replicas pe hi rahein taaki scale bana rahe.
why.en: This is replication lag. Route only the affected user/time window to the primary; keep other reads on replicas to keep scaling.

q.hi: Swiggy orders sharding: zyada tar queries "mere orders" (by user) hain. Best shard key?
q.en: Sharding Swiggy orders: most queries are "my orders" (by user). Best shard key?

hi: created_at
city
hash(user_id)
order_status
en: created_at
city
hash(user_id)
order_status

why.hi: user_id high-cardinality hai aur main query ek shard pe jaati hai. created_at se latest shard hot hota hai, city skewed hai (Bangalore bada), status me bas kuch values hain.
why.en: user_id is high-cardinality and the main query hits one shard. created_at makes the newest shard hot, city is skewed (Bangalore is huge), status has few values.

q.hi: hash(key) % N ki jagah consistent hashing kyu?
q.en: Why consistent hashing instead of hash(key) % N?

hi: Consistent hashing se hot keys khatam ho jaati hain
Isme replication ki zarurat nahi
Ye range queries fast kar deta hai
Node add/remove pe sirf ~K/N keys move hoti hain; modulo me N badalte hi zyada tar keys move ho jaati hain
en: Consistent hashing eliminates hot keys
It removes the need for replication
It makes range queries fast
Adding/removing a node moves only ~K/N keys; with modulo, changing N moves most keys

why.hi: Ring pe har node ka hissa fixed hai; naya node sirf apne neighbour ka hissa leta hai. Virtual nodes load ko even karte hain. Hot key phir bhi hot rehti hai.
why.en: On the ring each node owns a slice; a new node takes only part of a neighbour's slice. Virtual nodes even out load. A hot key stays hot.

q.hi: Orders user_id se sharded hain. Restaurant owner dashboard ko "mere restaurant ke aaj ke orders" chahiye, bahut baar. Best approach?
q.en: Orders are sharded by user_id. The restaurant dashboard needs "today's orders for my restaurant", very often. Best approach?

hi: restaurant_id se sharded alag table/index rakho, CDC/events se async fill karo
Har request pe saare shards pe scatter-gather query
Shard key ko restaurant_id kar do aur user queries scatter-gather
Saare orders ek single unsharded table me wapas le aao
en: Keep a separate table/index sharded by restaurant_id, filled asynchronously via CDC/events
Scatter-gather across all shards on every request
Switch the shard key to restaurant_id and scatter-gather user queries
Move all orders back into one unsharded table

why.hi: Ek shard key sirf ek access pattern ko serve karti hai. Doosre frequent pattern ke liye denormalized copy (global secondary index jaisa) rakho; thoda lag acceptable.
why.en: A shard key serves one access pattern. For a second frequent pattern keep a denormalized copy (like a global secondary index); a little lag is acceptable.

q.hi: User ki 200 MB video upload: backend se bytes proxy karne ki jagah S3 pre-signed URL kyu?
q.en: A user uploads a 200 MB video: why an S3 pre-signed URL instead of proxying bytes through the backend?

hi: Pre-signed URL se object public ho jaata hai hamesha ke liye
Isse upload ke bina hi file S3 me aa jaati hai
Client seedha S3 pe time-limited signed URL se upload karta hai; backend bandwidth bachti hai aur AWS credentials client ko nahi milte
Pre-signed URL file ko automatically compress karta hai
en: The pre-signed URL makes the object public forever
The file reaches S3 without uploading
The client uploads straight to S3 with a time-limited signed URL; backend bandwidth is saved and no AWS credentials reach the client
The pre-signed URL compresses the file automatically

why.hi: Backend sirf permission (bucket, key, method, expiry) sign karta hai. URL expire hone ke baad bekaar; object private hi rehta hai.
why.en: The backend only signs a permission (bucket, key, method, expiry). After expiry the URL is useless; the object stays private.

q.hi: S3 multipart upload ke baare me kaunsa sahi hai?
q.en: Which is true about S3 multipart upload?

hi: Single PUT se 50 GB tak upload ho sakta hai, multipart optional hai
Parts sirf sequential order me upload ho sakte hain
CompleteMultipartUpload ke bina bhi object visible ho jaata hai
Parts parallel upload ho sakte hain, fail hua part hi retry hota hai; last part chhod ke har part kam se kam 5 MB
en: A single PUT can upload up to 50 GB, so multipart is optional
Parts must be uploaded strictly in sequence
The object becomes visible even without CompleteMultipartUpload
Parts can upload in parallel and only a failed part is retried; every part except the last is at least 5 MB

why.hi: Single PUT ki limit 5 GB hai; usse bade ke liye multipart zaroori (max 10,000 parts, object 5 TB tak). Complete call ke baad hi object banta hai.
why.en: A single PUT is capped at 5 GB; beyond that multipart is required (max 10,000 parts, objects up to 5 TB). The object exists only after the Complete call.

q.hi: Aaj S3 me PUT (naya object ya overwrite) ke turant baad GET karne pe kya milta hai?
q.en: Today, what does a GET right after a PUT (new object or overwrite) on S3 return?

hi: Naya data: S3 strong read-after-write consistency deta hai (Dec 2020 se)
Kuch minute tak purana data mil sakta hai (eventual consistency)
404 jab tak replication complete na ho
Overwrite pe hamesha purana version jab tak cache clear na ho
en: The new data: S3 offers strong read-after-write consistency (since Dec 2020)
Possibly old data for a few minutes (eventual consistency)
404 until replication completes
Always the old version on overwrite until a cache is cleared

why.hi: S3 ab PUT, overwrite, DELETE aur LIST sab pe strong consistency deta hai. Purane interview answers "eventual" bolte the; CDN cache alag cheez hai.
why.en: S3 now gives strong consistency for PUT, overwrite, DELETE and LIST. Older interview answers said "eventual"; a CDN cache is a separate matter.

q.hi: S3 bill badh raha hai par bucket me dikhne wale objects ka size utna nahi. Bahut se mobile uploads beech me fail hote hain. Likely cause aur fix?
q.en: The S3 bill keeps rising but visible objects do not add up. Many mobile uploads fail midway. Likely cause and fix?

hi: Pre-signed URLs ka alag charge lagta hai; URLs kam banao
Incomplete multipart uploads ke parts store ho ke charge hote rehte hain; lifecycle rule AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload lagao
Versioning band hai isliye duplicates bante hain
S3 failed PUTs ko Glacier me move karta hai
en: Pre-signed URLs are billed separately; generate fewer URLs
Parts of incomplete multipart uploads stay stored and billed; add the AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload lifecycle rule
Versioning is off so duplicates are created
S3 moves failed PUTs to Glacier

why.hi: Jo multipart upload complete/abort nahi hua, uske parts listing me object ki tarah nahi dikhte par storage bill hote hain. Lifecycle rule N din baad unhe saaf karta hai.
why.en: Parts of a multipart upload never completed or aborted do not show as objects but are billed as storage. A lifecycle rule cleans them up after N days.

q.hi: Network partition ke time Cassandra (default settings) kya prefer karta hai?
q.en: During a network partition, what does Cassandra (default settings) favour?

hi: Consistency (CP); writes reject karta hai
Dono, kyunki CAP Cassandra pe apply nahi hota
Partition ke time poora cluster read-only
Availability (AP); consistency level tunable hai
en: Consistency (CP); it rejects writes
Both, because CAP does not apply to Cassandra
The whole cluster goes read-only during a partition
Availability (AP); consistency level is tunable

why.hi: Leaderless Cassandra replicas available rehte hue writes leta hai (hinted handoff, read repair). QUORUM/ALL rakhoge to zyada consistent par kam available.
why.en: Leaderless Cassandra keeps accepting writes on available replicas (hinted handoff, read repair). With QUORUM/ALL you get more consistency, less availability.

q.hi: Order list page: 1 query se 100 orders, phir loop me har order ka restaurant alag query se. Isse kya kehte hain aur fix?
q.en: Order list page: 1 query fetches 100 orders, then one query per order for its restaurant in a loop. What is this and the fix?

hi: N+1 query problem; JOIN ya ek batch WHERE id IN (...) query
Deadlock; isolation level badhao
Cache stampede; TTL random karo
Hot partition; shard karo
en: The N+1 query problem; use a JOIN or one batched WHERE id IN (...) query
A deadlock; raise the isolation level
A cache stampede; randomise TTLs
A hot partition; add sharding

why.hi: 101 round trips ki jagah 1-2 queries. ORMs me eager loading (include/join fetch) se fix hota hai.
why.en: 1-2 queries instead of 101 round trips. In ORMs fix it with eager loading (include/join fetch).

q.hi: Order history: ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 20 OFFSET 100000 bahut slow hai. Better?
q.en: Order history: ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 20 OFFSET 100000 is very slow. Better option?

hi: OFFSET ko chhote batches me tod do
Keyset/cursor pagination: WHERE (created_at, id) < (:last_ts, :last_id) ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT 20
SELECT COUNT(*) pehle chalao phir OFFSET
ORDER BY hata do
en: Split the OFFSET into smaller batches
Keyset/cursor pagination: WHERE (created_at, id) < (:last_ts, :last_id) ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT 20
Run SELECT COUNT(*) first, then OFFSET
Drop the ORDER BY

why.hi: OFFSET ko 100000 rows padh ke phekni padti hain. Cursor index se seedha last position pe seek karta hai; id tie-breaker duplicates/skips rokta hai.
why.en: OFFSET must read and discard 100000 rows. A cursor seeks straight to the last position via the index; the id tie-breaker prevents duplicates/skips.

q.hi: Optimistic locking: UPDATE products SET stock = ?, version = version + 1 WHERE id = 7 AND version = 3; ne 0 rows affected return kiya. Matlab?
q.en: Optimistic locking: UPDATE products SET stock = ?, version = version + 1 WHERE id = 7 AND version = 3; returned 0 rows affected. What does it mean?

hi: Row lock lag gaya hai, thodi der me apne aap ho jaayega
Query syntax galat hai
Kisi aur ne beech me row update kar di (version ab 3 nahi); latest row padh ke retry karo ya conflict dikhao
Update ho gaya par count galat report hua
en: A row lock is held and it will apply by itself shortly
The query syntax is wrong
Someone else updated the row in between (version is no longer 3); re-read the latest row and retry or report a conflict
The update applied but the count was misreported

why.hi: Optimistic locking lock nahi leta; version match na hone pe write skip hota hai. Low-contention cases me achha; high contention me retries badhte hain, tab pessimistic lock socho.
why.en: Optimistic locking takes no lock; a version mismatch skips the write. Good under low contention; with high contention retries pile up, so consider pessimistic locks.
